label: Search Frame (portal-frame iframe)
summary: Grab the Employee Search sidebar iframe with a dynamic session-dependent name.
note: Returns a FrameLocator (not a Locator); used as the SearchRoot context for all search selectors. iframe name suffix changes each session (name^="portal-frame-"). Inferred scrape kind — this is a container/context provider, not a directly interactive element.

label: WFD Loading Overlay
summary: WFD full-page loading overlay — wait for it to be hidden before clicking.
note: CSS multi-selector: .wfd-loading-overlay, [data-wfd-loading], .wfd-modal-overlay, .wfd-busy-indicator. Used as a wait/probe (waitFor hidden) before clicks; not directly interacted with. NEEDS LIVE RE-VERIFY 2026-06-17.

label: Navbar — Employee Search Button
summary: Open the Employee Search sidebar.

label: Search — Employee Name/ID Input (fill)
summary: Search textbox — accepts employee name or ID; resolved iframe-or-top-level.
accessibleName: Search by Employee Name or ID
note: Accepts SearchRoot (FrameLocator | Page). The sidebar renders inside the portal-frame iframe on fresh load but top-level after timecard navigation; navigate.ts resolves the live root via resolveSearchRoot.

label: Search — Employee Name/ID Input (scrape)
summary: Read current value of the employee search textbox.
accessibleName: Search by Employee Name or ID
note: Accepts SearchRoot (FrameLocator | Page). See fill variant for iframe/page duality note.

label: Search — Submit Button
summary: Search submit button (exact name to distinguish from other Search buttons).
note: getByRole with exact:true to avoid matching other Search-named buttons on the page.

label: Search — No Results Text
summary: "There are no items to display" text — no-results probe.
note: Used to detect empty search results via waitFor. Probed in a race against firstResultCheckbox/firstResultSlat in resolveSearchResult.

label: Search — First Result Checkbox (Select Item)
summary: First result's "Select Item" checkbox — checking it selects the employee, enabling the Go To button.
note: Targeted precisely by accessible name "Select Item" — do NOT union with bare input[type=checkbox], which would also match the "Select All" header checkbox. The backing native input is visually hidden (zero-size); found-detection uses attached state, not visible state.

label: Search — First Result Row (fallback)
summary: First result row fallback — menuitemradio or row[role=row]; clicking also selects the employee.
note: .or() fallback chain: getByRole('menuitemradio') or locator('[role=row]') .first(). Accepts SearchRoot.

label: Search — First Result Slat (found probe)
summary: First result SLAT — a "somebody showed up" signal for found-detection.
note: Kept TIGHT (no [role=row] fallback) so a header/placeholder row cannot false-positive a not-found search into found. Used in Promise.any([...]) race with firstResultCheckbox for found-detection in resolveSearchResult. NEEDS LIVE RE-VERIFY 2026-06-22.

label: Search — Close Sidebar Button
summary: Close the Employee Search sidebar.
note: Accepts SearchRoot.

label: Go To Menu — Go To Button (page-level)
summary: Employee Search panel's "Go To" dropdown at the top-level page render.
note: MUST be scoped to the Quick Find slide-out to avoid hitting the timecard toolbar's always-enabled "Go to" button. Primary: #goToDropdownButton; fallback: .quick-find-content scoped /go to/i role button. .or() chain, .first(). NEEDS LIVE RE-VERIFY 2026-06-22.

label: Go To Menu — Go To Button (portal-frame iframe)
summary: Employee Search panel's "Go To" dropdown inside the portal-frame iframe render.
note: Same slide-out scoping as goToButtonOnPage but takes a FrameLocator argument. NEEDS LIVE RE-VERIFY 2026-06-22.

label: Go To Menu — Timecard Menu Item
summary: Timecard menu item in the open Go To dropdown.
note: Name anchored to /^\s*timecards?\s*$/i — bare substring /timecard/i matched page-chrome ('Employee timecards' title) causing stale-element failures. .or() chain covers: frame option, page option, frame menuitem, page menuitem. Anchoring added 2026-06-24.

label: Timecard — Pay Period Trigger Button
summary: Pay-period trigger button — text varies ("Current Pay Period", "Previous Pay Period", or a date range).
note: Regex name matches current, previous, or date-range display. .first() in case multiple match.

label: Timecard — Previous Pay Period Option
summary: Previous Pay Period option inside an open period dropdown.

label: Timecard — Select Range Button
summary: "Select range" button to switch to custom date range.

label: Timecard — Start Date Input (fill)
summary: Start date input for custom range — NATIVE <input type=date>, value as ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
note: Targeted by id #startDateTimeInput. MUST fill with ISO YYYY-MM-DD — MM/DD/YYYY silently reverts to today (OBS-006); per-key typing fights browser segment mask (ISS-B05). Calendar fallback path available in setRangeDate.

label: Timecard — Start Date Input (scrape)
summary: Read the current start date value from the custom range input.
note: Value is ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Targeted by id #startDateTimeInput.

label: Timecard — End Date Input (fill)
summary: End date input for custom range — NATIVE <input type=date>, value as ISO YYYY-MM-DD.
note: Targeted by id #endDateTimeInput. Same fill rules as startDateInput: ISO only, no masked typing.

label: Timecard — End Date Input (scrape)
summary: Read the current end date value from the custom range input.
note: Value is ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Targeted by id #endDateTimeInput.

label: Timecard — Calendar Month/Year Header
summary: Moment-picker month/year header (e.g. "Jun 2026") — read to know which way to step the calendar.
note: CSS locator: th.js-moment-picker-parent-view .first(). Read its text to determine navigation direction for calendarPrevMonth / calendarNextMonth.

label: Timecard — Calendar Previous Month Arrow
summary: Moment-picker "Previous month" arrow button.

label: Timecard — Calendar Next Month Arrow
summary: Moment-picker "Next month" arrow button.

label: Timecard — Calendar Day Cell
summary: Moment-picker day cell for a specific date — click to select a day in the range picker.
note: Takes a runtime name param (string | RegExp) matching the full-date aria-label (e.g. 'Monday, June 11, 2026'). .and(td.js-moment-picker-item:not(.out-of-month)) prevents matching adjacent-month trailing days.

label: Timecard — Apply Button
summary: Apply button for the custom date range.
